data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq futures climb on optimism ahead of Anthropic's market debut
data.description:
* Futures up: Dow 0.67%, S&P 500 1.25%, Nasdaq 2.15%

* Anthropic IPO pricing lifts AI-linked stocks

* Cybersecurity firms up after Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) lifts FY27 forecast

(Updates prices throughout, adds analyst comments)

By Medha Singh and Utkarsh Hathi

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures rose more than 2% on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around beaten-down AI stocks.

Anthropic priced its upsized offering at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record that valued the AI lab at about $1.5 trillion. It will begin trading on the Nasdaq later in the day.

The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies, as investors fretted over stretched valuations, hefty spending on AI infrastructure and the fallout from Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit.

"A strong debut is the tonic that the market needs after such a volatile period... it tells us that investor demand is still there," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem."

Hyperscalers Amazon and Alphabet, also among the investors in the AI startup, added 2.2% and 3.9%, respectively, in premarket trading.

Chipmakers also gained, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) up 1.8% after falling for five straight sessions through Wednesday, as upbeat revenue forecast did little to uplift sentiment.

Intel ( INTC ), Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Micron , and Marvell ( MRVL ) rose between 3.2% and 4.6%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius gained 4.8% each, while data center-related companies IREN ( IREN ) and Applied Digital ( APLD ) climbed 5.4% each.

At 05:48 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 335 points, or 0.67%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 92 points, or 1.25%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 585.5 points, or 2.15%.

The S&P 500 logged its fifth consecutive session of decline on Wednesday, with Hawkish minutes from the US Federal Reserve's latest meeting also weighing on sentiment.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, according to the minutes from the central bank's October policy meeting, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and could call for tighter policy.

Investors will now parse remarks from several Fed officials due later on Thursday.

Traders are pricing in near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Among other movers, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) shares jumped 10% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue forecast, helping drive gains of 4.5% to 7% in peers CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) , Cloudflare ( NET ), Okta ( OKTA ) and Zscaler ( ZS ).

Walmart ( WMT ) is scheduled to report quarterly earnings before the opening bell on Thursday.

(Reporting by Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by Ronojoy Mazumdar and Shilpi Majumdar)

data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX futures gain as oil, gold edge up; Anthropic debut in focus
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Futures tied to Canada's commodity-heavy stock index rose on Thursday as oil and gold prices recouped some losses, while investors awaited Anthropic's market debut due later in the day.

December futures on the S&P/TSX 60 index were up 0.43% at 5:52 a.m. ET (1055 GMT).

* Gold gained on bargain hunting and short covering with spot gold up 0.4% after hitting a 14-month low in the previous session

* Brent crude was little changed after edging up 0.2% earlier in the session, as worries about Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz offset expectations for a surplus

* Investors are closely watching for Anthropic's much-awaited debut after the Claude chatbot maker priced its IPO above the marketed range, pulling off the largest offering on record

* Anthropic's IPO values the company at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, with its first day of trading expected to serve as a key test of investor appetite for the AI sector

* On Wednesday, Canada's main stock index fell more than 2% to a five-month low, as lower oil and metal prices triggered a selloff in the energy and materials sectors

* Separately, Alberta, Canada's main energy-producing province announced new legislation aimed at enhancing protections for communities and landowners while still encouraging data center development and oil and gas growth

data.title: Maximus Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Results for Fiscal Year 2026
data.description:
Completes Agile Defense acquisition, delivers earnings above guidance, and establishes fiscal year 2027 guidance

TYSONS, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Maximus ( MMS ) , a leading provider of government services, reported financial results for the three months and year ended September 30, 2026. The acquisition of Agile Defense, LLC (Agile Defense) was completed on November 18, 2026.

Highlights for fiscal year 2026 include:

  • Full year revenue of $5.23 billion, landing within the guidance range.
  • Full year operating margin of 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.2%, along with diluted earnings per share of $7.27 and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.24, which exceeded the top end of guidance and increased 12.0% over the prior year on an adjusted earnings per share basis.
  • Full year cash flows from operating activities of $112 million and free cash flow of $69 million. Subsequent to fiscal year-end, collections totaled more than $330 million from a major customer.
  • Repurchases of Maximus ( MMS ) common stock totaling approximately $192 million during fiscal year 2026.
  • Establishes fiscal year 2027 guidance of $5.45 billion to $5.65 billion of revenue, adjusted diluted earnings per share of $7.50 to $8.00, and free cash flow of $700 million to $800 million; fiscal year 2027 guidance reflects the absence of an estimated $1.05 per share of benefit recognized in fiscal year 2026 attributable to a specific program, which is discussed further below.
  • A quarterly cash dividend of $0.33 per share payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026.

"Fiscal year 2026 reflected the benefits of disciplined execution, technology-enabled productivity enhancements, and thoughtful capital allocation," said Bruce Caswell, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Throughout the year, we continued deploying automation and AI-enabled solutions across our operations, improving efficiency, strengthening profitability, and delivering meaningful outcomes for customers. These efforts contributed to adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.24, representing 12.0% growth over the prior year and performance above the top end of our most recently updated guidance range."

Caswell continued, "Subsequent to fiscal year-end, we completed the acquisition of Agile Defense, which significantly expands our position in defense and national security markets and enhances our portfolio of technology-enabled capabilities. As we enter fiscal year 2027, we remain focused on integrating Agile Defense, growing existing customer relationships, executing on opportunities associated with recent policy initiatives, and further advancing our leadership in AI-enabled solutions and technology innovation."

Agile Defense Acquisition Close

On November 18, 2026, Maximus ( MMS ) completed its acquisition of Agile Defense, a provider of mission-focused technology solutions supporting customers across the Department of War, Intelligence Community, homeland security, and civilian agencies.

The acquisition expands Maximus' ( MMS ) presence in defense and national security markets while adding differentiated capabilities in cybersecurity, digital modernization, software and analytics, cloud solutions, and AI-enabled mission support services. The transaction further diversifies the U.S. Federal Service's portfolio, enhances access to strategically important customers, and increases exposure to attractive markets with favorable long-term growth characteristics.

Agile Defense is expected to contribute approximately ten months of revenue during fiscal year 2027 and is included in the fiscal year 2027 guidance.

Consolidated Fiscal Year 2026 Results

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $5.23 billion, compared to $5.43 billion reported for the prior fiscal year. As previously discussed, fiscal year 2025 benefited from elevated natural disaster support activities and temporary clinical program volume surges that did not recur at the same level during fiscal year 2026. Revenue finished within the fiscal year 2026 guidance range and was consistent with our expectations throughout the year.

For fiscal year 2026, the operating margin was 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin was 14.2%, compared to 9.7% and 12.9%, respectively, in the prior fiscal year. The improvement reflects technology-enabled productivity enhancements, including automation initiatives, disciplined cost management efforts, and strong operational performance.

Diluted earnings per share were $7.27 and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $8.24 for fiscal year 2026. This compares to $5.51 and $7.36, respectively, in the prior fiscal year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share exceeded the top end of the most recently updated guidance range for fiscal year 2026 and increased 12.0% over the prior year. Earnings growth was driven principally by improved operating performance reflected in the margin improvement and the benefit of capital deployment actions, including share repurchases.

U.S. Federal Services Segment

U.S. Federal Services Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was approximately $2.99 billion. Prior fiscal year revenue of $3.07 billion benefited from nearly $100 million of elevated natural disaster support activity and temporary clinical volume surges that did not recur at the same level during fiscal year 2026.

The segment operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 18.1%, compared to 15.3% reported for the prior fiscal year. Margin expansion was driven by technology-enabled efficiencies, productivity improvements, strong execution across core program areas, and favorable operating leverage generated through automation initiatives deployed throughout the fiscal year. Together, these factors helped create opportunities to efficiently process higher volumes and improve profitability, such as incentive payments on the Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Disability Examination (VA MDE) program during the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026.

Fourth quarter results of fiscal year 2026 reflected the previously disclosed customer-directed modification to the VA MDE program regarding performance incentives. The fourth quarter also benefited from strong performance across the clinical portfolio, which is expected to moderate in fiscal year 2027.

U.S. Services Segment

U.S. Services Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $1.68 billion, compared to $1.76 billion reported for the prior fiscal year. Revenue performance was generally consistent with expectations and reflected varying volumes across several contract areas. Revenue trends improved throughout fiscal year 2026, culminating in positive organic growth in the fourth quarter.

The segment operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 9.1%, compared to 9.7% reported in the prior fiscal year. Fiscal year 2026 results included a $6.9 million non-cash impairment charge related to a software asset developed and capitalized for a specific customer.

We continue to see encouraging demand indicators associated with Medicaid community engagement requirements, program integrity activities, eligibility administration, and other state government initiatives that are expected to support future growth opportunities.

Outside the U.S. Segment

Outside the U.S. Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $557 million, compared to $600 million reported for the prior fiscal year. The revenue decrease was attributable to previously divested businesses as well as lower revenue across several employment services and clinical programs amidst certain customer-specific challenges.

The segment reported a modest operating loss, primarily reflecting the lower revenue across those employment services and clinical programs. Maximus ( MMS ) continues to focus on driving profitable growth through disciplined bid selection, operational improvements, and successful conversion of its sales pipeline.

Sales and Pipeline

Signed contract awards for fiscal year 2026 totaled $2.51 billion, and contracts pending (awarded but unsigned) totaled $1.86 billion at September 30, 2026. The book-to-bill ratio at September 30, 2026, was 0.5x on a trailing twelve-month basis and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio improved to approximately 1.0x, representing the strongest quarterly award performance of fiscal year 2026.

The fourth quarter book-to-bill ratio was enabled by a signed contract award for a significant state Medicaid contract renewal representing more than $800 million of total contract value over a ten-year period. Included in the contracts pending balance are two recently awarded state Medicaid contract renewals totaling approximately $528 million of total contract value.

The total sales pipeline at September 30, 2026, was $44.8 billion (comprised of approximately $4.01 billion in proposals pending, $1.61 billion in proposals in preparation, and $39.2 billion in opportunities tracking). New work opportunities represent approximately 61% of the total sales pipeline, and U.S. Federal Services Segment opportunities represent approximately 58% of the total sales pipeline.

During fiscal year 2026, Maximus ( MMS ) achieved a recompete win rate of approximately 89%, reflecting the strength of its customer relationships, operational performance, and technology-enabled service delivery model.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flows

At September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $280 million, and gross debt was $1.61 billion. The ratio of debt, net of allowed cash, to consolidated EBITDA for the full year ended September 30, 2026, as calculated in accordance with our credit agreement, was 1.8x.

Following the completion of the Agile Defense acquisition, our pro forma leverage ratio is expected to be approximately 2.3x, remaining within Maximus' ( MMS ) targeted leverage range of 2x to 3x and preserving financial flexibility for future capital allocation priorities.

For fiscal year 2026, cash flows from operating activities totaled $112 million and free cash flow was $69 million, enabled by $278 million of free cash flow for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. This compares to $429 million and $366 million, respectively, in the prior fiscal year.

Days sales outstanding, or DSO, were 93 days at September 30, 2026, compared to 98 days at June 30, 2026. Subsequent to fiscal year-end and through November 13, 2026, we collected more than $330 million from a major customer that had been anticipated in our fiscal year 2026 guidance. As a result, a portion of cash generation expected during fiscal year 2026 shifted into fiscal year 2027 guidance due to timing-related factors rather than collection concerns. During fiscal year 2026, we repurchased approximately 2.6 million shares of Maximus ( MMS ) common stock totaling approximately $192 million. As of November 13, 2026, the full $400 million balance from the most recent Board of Directors authorization remains available.

On October 5, 2026, our Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.33 for each share of our common stock outstanding. The dividend is payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026.

Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance

Maximus ( MMS ) is establishing fiscal year 2027 guidance.

We expect revenue to range between $5.45 billion and $5.65 billion. The outlook includes approximately ten months of contribution from Agile Defense and reflects expectations for continued growth opportunities across defense and national security markets, state government programs, and technology-enabled services.

Maximus ( MMS ) expects adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 12.8% for fiscal year 2027 and adjusted diluted earnings per share to range between $7.50 and $8.00 per share.

This guidance assumes no incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts during fiscal year 2027. Fiscal year 2026 included incentive-related revenue and profit equal to an estimated $75 million and $1.05 adjusted earnings per share, respectively, total contribution across the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026. Excluding the incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts to the fiscal year 2026, the midpoint of our adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance represents growth of approximately 8%.

We expect free cash flow to range between $700 million and $800 million. The outlook reflects DSO returning to the historical range of 60-70 days and includes the benefit of collections that shifted beyond fiscal year-end.

For fiscal year 2027, Maximus ( MMS ) expects amortization of intangible assets of approximately $96 million, depreciation and amortization of property, equipment and capitalized software of approximately $55 million, interest expense of approximately $110 million, an effective tax rate of approximately 25%, and weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 52.1 million.

Conference Call and Webcast Information

Maximus ( MMS ) will host a conference call today, November 19, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET.

The call is open to the public and available by webcast or by phone at:

877.407.8289 (Domestic) / +1.201.689.8341 (International)

For those unable to listen to the live call, a recording of the webcast will be available on investor.maximus.com.

About Maximus ( MMS )

As a leading strategic partner to government, Maximus ( MMS ) helps improve the delivery of public services amid complex technology, health, economic, and social challenges. Maximus ( MMS ) provides tech-enabled services to government agencies, including innovative business process management and technology solutions that are designed to improve outcomes for the public and create higher levels of productivity and efficiency of government-sponsored programs. With a deep understanding of program service delivery, acute insights that achieve operational excellence, and an extensive awareness of the needs of the people being served, our employees advance the critical missions of our partners. For more information, visit maximus.com.

data.title: Willis Lease Finance Corporation Expands Fleet with Acquisition of Two Airbus A320 Aircraft
data.description:
COCONUT CREEK, Fla., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC ) (the "Company"), the leading lessor of commercial aircraft engines and global provider of aviation services, today announces that it has completed the acquisition of two Airbus A320 aircraft.

The acquisitions complement the Company’s core engine leasing business and reflect its continued commitment to strategically expanding its aviation asset portfolio to meet growing customer demand.

“Demand for assets and flexible leasing solutions remains exceptionally strong in today’s environment,” said Austin C. Willis, President & Chief Executive Officer of Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC ). “We continue to grow our portfolio and strengthen our ability to serve airline customers around the world. The addition of both a new-generation A320neo and an A320ceo reflects our disciplined approach to investing in diverse assets.”

Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC )

Willis Lease Finance Corporation ( WLFC ) leases large and regional spare commercial aircraft engines and aircraft to airlines, aircraft engine manufacturers and maintenance, repair, and overhaul providers worldwide. These leasing activities are integrated with engine and aircraft trading, engine lease pools, and asset management services through Willis Mitsui & Co. Asset Management Limited, as well as various end-of-life solutions for engines and aviation materials provided through Willis Aeronautical Services, Inc. Through Willis Engine Repair Center®, Jet Centre by Willis, and Willis Aviation Services Limited, the Company’s service offerings include Part 145 engine maintenance, aircraft line and base maintenance, aircraft disassembly, parking and storage, airport FBO and ground and cargo handling services.

data.title: Anthropic's historic debut to put AI's promise and peril to Wall St test
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO brings to Wall Street an avatar of a sector that proponents herald as an economic panacea, while detractors warn it has stoked a market bubble and could ultimately threaten humanity itself.

More immediately, the Claude chatbot maker's debut after securing a $1.5 trillion valuation in the IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia ( NVDA ), signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week.

The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to the sector, even as a rocky market reception for Nvidia ( NVDA ) results which looked strong at first blush, signals the euphoria around the sector has cooled.

"I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia ( NVDA ) gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut.

AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections.

Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the incipient crushing debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.

An extramarital-affair scandal involving Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO and a spike in Treasury yields have further unnerved investors.

AN INDUSTRY BENCHMARK

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with its arch-rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing.

The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the roadshow. The additional $26 billion raised through a private placement takes the total haul to over $107 billion.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for about 28% of Anthropic's shares offered, or roughly $19 billion.

When it debuts on the Nasdaq later on Thursday, Anthropic will join the world's trillion-dollar club, alongside technology giants such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ).

The listing will also give retail investors a chance to pile into one of the AI industry's hottest names, potentially amplifying swings in the stock as trading begins.

The buzz has already spilled onto prediction markets, where traders are placing bets on everything from its opening pop to where the stock will close on its first day.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, some of the world's biggest CEOs, and political leaders split over its sustainability.

Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

"It doesn't have to be a bad company for it to be a bad investment at the IPO price," said Nic Puckrin, cross-asset analyst and founder of Coin Bureau.

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control.

Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade as questions over valuations, spending and returns weigh on sentiment.

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models over concerns that they pose cybersecurity threats and could be exploited by bad actors to target critical government and private infrastructure.

Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms, posing potentially "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Ragini Mathur; Editing by Christian Plumb and Arun Koyyur)

data.title: Alibaba tops revenue estimates on AI cloud growth; profit up on investment gains
data.description:
* Quarterly revenue reaches 271.52 billion yuan, topping estimates

* Non-GAAP net income rises 92% to 19.9 billion yuan

* AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue jumps 53% to 60.97 billion yuan

(Recasts and adds profit, free cash flow, AI computing and cloud growth and investor concerns in paragraphs 1-6)

By Jaspreet Singh and Casey Hall

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Alibaba ( BABA ) beat estimates for September-quarter revenue on Thursday as demand for its AI cloud services surged, while investment gains helped more than triple reported profit.

China's biggest e-commerce company by market share said revenue from AI cloud and computing services jumped 53%, highlighting the growing payoff from heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and products.

"This quarter, our business delivered strong growth in both revenue and earnings because of our strategic focus on AI + Cloud growth and profit sustainability in Alibaba E-commerce Group," Chief Financial Officer Toby Xu said.

Excluding investment gains and other items, non-GAAP net income leapt 92% to 19.9 billion yuan ($2.99 billion), helped by stronger profitability and narrowing losses in its quick-commerce business.

Alibaba's ( BABA ) shares are down about 40% this year, as investors worry about weak consumer demand in China and rising spending on AI and cloud infrastructure.

Free cash flow was an outflow of 34.47 billion yuan in the quarter, compared with an outflow of 21.84 billion yuan a year earlier. Alibaba ( BABA ) said the increase reflected higher spending on cloud infrastructure, partly offset by lower losses at Taobao Instant Commerce and higher customer pre-payments for cloud services.

Capital expenditure rose 60% to 50.48 billion yuan.

Alibaba ( BABA ) reported quarterly revenue of 271.52 billion yuan, ahead of analysts' average estimate of 269.81 billion yuan, according to LSEG data.

AI cloud and computing services revenue totalled 60.97 billion yuan. Alibaba ( BABA ) has sharply increased spending on AI infrastructure, proprietary models and applications, betting on the technology as a key growth driver.

Adjusted earnings per American Depositary Share were 8.10 yuan, below analysts' expectations of 11.16 yuan.

In September, Alibaba ( BABA ) unveiled plans to expand global data-centre capacity to more than 20 gigawatts by 2032 and said its next-generation Qwen 4 model was in training. Its chip-design unit T-Head, which confidentially filed for a Hong Kong listing earlier this month, also unveiled a new AI processor scheduled for commercial release in early 2027.

Alibaba ( BABA ) launched a $10 billion share placement in August, saying the proceeds would fund computing infrastructure and AI data centres.

The company recently reorganised its businesses into four main units: e-commerce, AI cloud and computing services, AI model applications and other businesses.

($1 = 6.6661 Chinese yuan renminbi)

(Reporting by Jaspreet Singh in Bengaluru and Casey Hall in Shanghai. Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Mark Potter)

data.title: GRAPHIC-The US IPO market is bigger than ever, but not busier
data.description:
* Anthropic, SpaceX mega IPOs define an uneven year for listings

* Broader IPO market still awaits bigger breakthrough

* Analysts see pipelines full, but deals pushed to 2027

* Volatile markets sideline issuers in the fall

By Manya Saini

Nov 19 (Reuters) - Widely tipped to come roaring back in 2026 after years of sluggish activity, the US IPO market has proved a study in contrasts, with fundraising shattering records while the number of companies going public stays well below historical highs.

Anthropic's debut on Thursday is set to cap a year of blockbuster listings, but the headline fundraising figures tell only part of the story.

"It's the year of the mega IPO. The proceeds numbers alone makes 2026 look like a bigger year than it was," said Matt Kennedy, senior IPO market strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs.

"Based on deal activity, it's just the latest year in the gradual improvement of the IPO market since 2022."

MEGA IPOS STEAL THE SHOW

Two mega IPOs have powered fundraising past the 2021 record. Anthropic, the AI lab behind the Claude chatbot, raised $81.3 billion in its IPO, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion offering to set a record for the world's largest IPO.

SpaceX's proceeds subsequently climbed after underwriters exercised the option to purchase additional shares. Anthropic's total could also rise further if its underwriters do the same.

FEWER COMPANIES JOIN THE PARTY

Underneath the record fundraising, the IPO market has been much quieter. Listings have slowed sharply in the second half of the year as the AI trade soured, bond yields climbed and expectations of interest-rate hikes weighed on investor sentiment.

"SpaceX and Anthropic alone will account for about two-thirds of this year's proceeds, so the headline figure overstates how broad the recovery really is," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

A SELECTIVE MARKET

Much of the activity has been concentrated in sectors such as technology, aerospace and biotech. For others, the window to go public remains elusive.

"I would describe 2026 as a selective reopening rather than a broad-based revival. Many companies that held back this year will be looking to 2027," Muehlbauer said.

The uneven recovery and investor attention on mega offerings have left smaller companies struggling to find room in the market, prompting many prospective issuers to wait for a more favorable window.

Bank of America ( BAC ) CEO Brian Moynihan said this week that some deals are being pushed into 2027 as Anthropic's listing crowds out smaller issuers.

Capital markets activity by the end of the year "will be up a chunk, but it's been very bumpy," Moynihan said in a Bloomberg Television interview, adding that the pipeline remains full.

MAPPING SENTIMENT

An index tracking IPO stocks has underperformed the broader S&P 500 so far this year, suggesting investors remain selective even as headline fundraising surges.

How stocks perform after their debut is closely watched to gauge investor appetite for new listings and whether companies are sustaining the momentum generated by their IPOs.

(Reporting by Manya Saini in Bengaluru; Editing by Pooja Desai)

data.title: Anthropic valued at $1.5 trillion as IPO raises record $81 billion
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record after increasing the size of its offering, in a deal that values the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion and defied concerns over AI and tech fundraising.

In a sign of strong investor demand, Anthropic priced its shares at $83 each, above its initial range of $70 to $78.

Reuters was first to report on Wednesday that Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to float, had increased the number of shares it was selling by about 19% to 980 million.

Anthropic's IPO eclipses the record-setting debut of Elon Musk's SpaceX in June. Its total deal size is $107.3 billion, including another $26 billion that Anthropic is raising through a private placement of shares, the filings showed.

Nasdaq futures rose nearly 2% on Thursday, bolstering expectations for a strong Anthropic debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks.

Chipmakers and cloud companies, which have raised hundreds of billions of dollars to fund their massive spending plans, have in recent weeks come under pressure due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs and the sudden exit of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Jensen Huang.

Anthropic has, meanwhile, faced questions about its outlook and ability to sustain rapid growth as competition intensifies.

Shares in Anthropic were up about 20% in over-the-counter grey market trading, brokerages IG Markets and CMC Markets said.

"Volumes are big," said Christopher Forbes, head of Asia and Middle East at CMC Markets in Singapore, adding that the brokerage was "seeing demand from all clients, retail to institutional" for the grey market stocks. 

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, which is awaiting a share allocation, said the Anthropic IPO was a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.  

"But one listing won't settle the debate. There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it'll take a few things to climb it. Once Anthropic reports publicly, it becomes one of the clearest tests of whether the economics of AI are holding up."

On a fully diluted basis, Anthropic's IPO values it at about $1.5 trillion, including securities such as stock options and restricted stock, and on a non-diluted basis at about $1.1 trillion.

US stock futures were up after Anthropic's IPO details were made public, while Asian tech stocks remained under pressure amid broader concerns about the AI trade. Anthropic is set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.    

A strong debut could give confidence to other companies waiting to tap public markets. Anthropic's closest rival, OpenAI, is expected to pursue a listing as early as next year.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) are lead underwriters for Anthropic's IPO, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate, and were also lead underwriters for SpaceX's listing.

SPENDING COMMITMENTS EXPOSE RISKS

Anthropic's growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent that has gained popularity among software developers. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing.

Underscoring its growing business foothold, Anthropic said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year.

But to sustain that growth, Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, nearly four times the amount spent a year earlier. 

It also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity.

Revenue rose to $16.96 billion in the third quarter, up 47% from the second. The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter. 

The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating ​items related to bonds convertible into its shares. 

Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners, including Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's Google, to train and operate AI models.

It warned that its computing providers and infrastructure partners depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity. 

"If such financing or support becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered," Anthropic said in an IPO filing. 

COMPETITION AND SAFETY CHALLENGES

Anthropic faces questions over how it will balance its commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety. 

CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks.

"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.

At the same time, competition is intensifying to be the leading provider of AI tools for businesses.

GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's latest flagship AI model, accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Claude Fable, data cited by Reuters in September showed. 

The competitive threat extends beyond the handful of companies developing the most powerful commercial models. A recent Capgemini study found 59% of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year as AI costs exceed budgets.

Meta Platforms, one of Anthropic's largest customers, has been looking to reduce its use of Anthropic's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, Reuters previously reported.

"Our thesis is that the vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier," said Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, which invested roughly $1.5 billion in Anthropic before its IPO. 

"Our bet is that Anthropic has the ingredients - that doesn't guarantee, but means that they arguably have the highest probability of remaining at the frontier." 

(Reporting by Echo Wang in New York; additional reporting by Ankur Banerjee and Gregor Stuart Hunter in Singapore; Editing by David Gaffen, Christian Plumb, Matthew Lewis, Sonali Paul and Alexander Smith)

Counter-UAS Market Drivers

Rising Drone-related Threats to Drive Market Growth

The primary driver of the counter-UAS market is the rapid increase in drone-related threats targeting military bases, borders, airports, ports, energy assets and other critical infrastructure. Low-cost unmanned aerial systems are now used for surveillance, smuggling, disruption and attack missions. Unauthorized drone activity is no longer viewed as an isolated security incident; it is treated as a persistent operational risk that demands continuous monitoring and rapid response. This is pushing defense agencies and infrastructure operators to invest in layered detection and mitigation systems.

Policy support is reinforcing this demand. In December 2024, the U.S. Department of Defense described unmanned aerial systems as an urgent and enduring threat to U.S. personnel, facilities and overseas assets, as well as a growing homeland security concern. Its strategy for countering unmanned systems aligned counter-UAS efforts with the Joint Counter-Small UAS Office and broader programs to protect critical installations and concentrated forces. Such strategic commitments translate into multi-year procurement budgets, providing strong visibility for counter-UAS market growth.

Counter-UAS Market Trends

AI-Enabled Layered Counter-UAS Architectures Drive Market Growth

A major trend in the counter-UAS market is the shift from standalone jamming solutions and sensor-only systems toward integrated, AI-enabled architectures. Faster, smaller and more coordinated drone threats require real-time classification and response rather than manual detection and delayed engagement. Buyers therefore prefer modular counter-UAS systems that combine radar, RF sensing, electro-optical/infrared payloads, detection and tracking, command-and-control and multiple mitigation options, and that can integrate with wider air-defense and base-security networks.

For instance, in December 2025, Lockheed Martin and Microsoft announced a collaboration to develop Sanctum, a next-generation counter-UAS capability that combines Lockheed Martin's mission-systems expertise with Microsoft's cloud and AI technologies. Partnerships between defense primes and technology companies are expected to accelerate software-led innovation across the counter-UAS industry.

Counter-UAS Market Restraints

Legal Restrictions on Active Mitigation to Restrain Market Growth

A key restraint on the counter-UAS market is the legal framework surrounding active mitigation, especially RF jamming, GNSS jamming/spoofing, cyber takeover and other solutions that interfere with communication links. These rules limit deployment by airports, private infrastructure operators, local authorities and some law enforcement agencies. As a result, many civilian buyers prioritize detection, tracking, electro-optical/infrared confirmation and command-and-control software first, while relying on government-led response models for neutralization. This slows the adoption of fully integrated counter-UAS solutions outside the defense sector.

Difficulty in Detecting Low-Emission and Small Drone Threats

Many small and low-emission drones are hard to detect, classify and defeat in cluttered environments. Commercial drones, autonomous drones and low-RF or "dark" drones can avoid basic RF-based detection, while birds, buildings, terrain, radio interference and dense urban activity create false alarms. Addressing these threats requires multi-sensor fusion and real-time decision support, which increases system cost and operational complexity. This higher cost can slow adoption among smaller defense units, airports and law enforcement agencies with limited budgets.

Homeland Security and Critical Infrastructure to Create Major Opportunities

The biggest future growth opportunity in the counter-UAS market lies beyond traditional defense. The Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East have made drone threats a central defense-planning issue. In Ukraine, the widespread use of low-cost drones, FPV systems, loitering munitions and reconnaissance UAVs has pushed armies toward layered counter-UAS systems. In the Middle East, one-way attack UAVs and Red Sea maritime attacks have increased demand for solutions that protect naval vessels, ports, air bases and energy infrastructure.

data.title: Dominion Dynamics and Telesat to develop ruggedized antennas to connect with Telesat Lightspeed
data.description:
OTTAWA, Ontario, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dominion Dynamics, an Ottawa-based defence technology company, and Telesat LEO ULC (Telesat LEO), a subsidiary of Telesat Corporation ( TSAT ) , one of the world’s largest satellite operators, have teamed up to develop ruggedized antennas intended to securely connect dismounted operators and uncrewed military platforms to the Telesat Lightspeed low Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.

“A soldier on patrol in Canada’s most remote regions and the uncrewed platforms they use should be connected to a Canadian network through equipment built here at home,” said Mitch Carkner, Chief Operating Officer at Dominion Dynamics. “While the CAF are the first intended users, the same technology could also serve the Canadian Rangers, the Canadian Coast Guard, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and emergency management in the High North.”

The $2.2-million project includes a contribution to Dominion Dynamics from the National Research Council’s Industrial Research Assistance Program and is intended to provide operators in the Arctic with a Canadian-controlled communications link to command centres across the country.

"Through investments in research and development, the Government of Canada is helping Canadian companies grow, innovate and develop technologies that strengthen Canada's economy and strategic capabilities. Congratulations to Dominion Dynamics and Telesat ( TSAT ) on this exciting collaboration,” said Hon. Mélanie Joly, Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions. “By developing advanced communications technologies here in Canada, these companies are helping build solutions for remote and northern environments while supporting Canadian innovation and creating new opportunities for growth."

Following this initial phase, Dominion intends to design and manufacture two user terminal prototypes: a compact unit light enough for a dismounted soldier to carry and a larger terminal built for uncrewed systems, including Dominion Scout. As Canada’s first sovereign Autonomous Collaborative Platform, Scout is an uncrewed combat aircraft being developed to extend the reach of Canada’s future fighter fleet.

The terminals are being designed with the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) in mind as the first potential customer. They are intended to operate in Arctic and expeditionary conditions, run on tactical power, and use open interfaces for integration with existing hardware. The prototypes are expected to undergo both cold-weather field trials, including service connectivity testing with Telesat Lightspeed.

“Kanata and Ottawa are home to some of Canada's most innovative technology and defence companies, and this partnership between Dominion Dynamics and Telesat ( TSAT ) demonstrates the strength of that ecosystem,” said Hon. Jenna Sudds, Member of Parliament for Kanata. “By bringing together local expertise to develop homegrown technologies for our Armed Forces, these companies are helping strengthen Canada's national security, sovereignty and defence capabilities. This is exactly the kind of innovation and collaboration we need to build Canada strong.”

Dominion Dynamics will lead the project as Prime contractor, with Telesat LEO acting as subcontractor. Together, the companies aim to deliver sovereign capability with intellectual property created and maintained in Canada.

“This is a great example of two Canadian companies combining their expertise in support of our national sovereignty,” said Stephen Hampton, Vice President, Canada and Sovereign Initiatives at Telesat ( TSAT ). “The collaboration reflects the growing strength of Canada's defence industrial base, and we look forward to working with Dominion to develop solutions that leverage the advanced capabilities we will integrate into the Telesat Lightspeed network."

Telesat Lightspeed is expected to enter high-latitude commercial service around the end of Q1 2028.

data.title: Gates to Acquire Nitta Interests in Five Asia-Pacific Markets, Concluding a Longstanding Joint Venture

The joint venture helped broaden Gates' reach to emerging economies in the Asia-Pacific region. The transaction positions Gates to operate in Asia-Pacific through a wholly owned platform and reinforces its long-term commitment to the region.

There are several important benefits for Gates that are anticipated to come from the transaction, including:

  • Significantly expands Gates' strategic flexibility to independently pursue growth initiatives in the Asia-Pacific region.

  • Simplifies Gates' financial reporting.

data.title: GTA VI frenzy spotlights potential insurance risks lurking in digital infrastructure
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Millions of gamers around the world have logged on for the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," arguably the century's most anticipated video game, offering a glimpse of the vast, interconnected digital infrastructure the global economy increasingly relies on.

No major disruption is expected from the rollout. But the scale of demand around one of the gaming industry's biggest releases underscores a broader risk for insurers: a failure at a shared cloud, payments or technology provider could affect thousands of businesses at once.

After 13 years in development and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, 'Grand Theft Auto VI' began rolling out globally on Thursday, drawing the kind of attention that few entertainment releases ever command.

But the fervour also underscores how much modern businesses depend on the digital infrastructure that makes such mass online activity possible, and the risks insurers face when that infrastructure fails.

"A launch of the scale of GTA VI is effectively a built-in stress test of the shared digital economy infrastructure," said Marcos Alvarez, managing director at Morningstar DBRS.

Insurers cover businesses against financial losses stemming from disruptions to their operations, including some caused by technology failures.

As companies increasingly rely on the same cloud providers, payment systems and digital platforms, a single outage could trigger claims from multiple policyholders at once, amplifying exposure.

Despite the frenzy surrounding the launch, any disruption on launch day or in the days that follow would not necessarily spell disaster for insurers, industry experts said.

"The recent technology outages have been a case in point with the gap between the economic cost and the actual insured loss being quite large due to policy limits, retentions, waiting periods, and coverage exclusions," Alvarez added.

Business interruption could be a major source of claims, but coverage could also extend to costs associated with data recovery, system restoration, cyberattacks and outages at third-party technology providers, depending on the policy.

"This is an area that is evolving rapidly for the insurance industry. Insurers are refining how they assess, model and manage these interconnected exposures," said Loretta Worters, a spokesperson for the Insurance Information Institute.

"That means looking beyond an individual company's cybersecurity protections to understand its reliance on third-party providers, the concentration of those dependencies across their portfolios and the potential for a single event to generate losses across multiple policyholders."

​

(Reporting by Manya Saini in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid)

data.title: Anthropic's rise from AI upstart to world's largest IPO
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic is set to make its Nasdaq debut later on Thursday after raising $81.3 billion in the world's largest IPO, making the Claude chatbot maker the first publicly traded frontier AI company.

The AI lab secured a $1.5 trillion valuation after pricing its shares above the marketed range, underscoring investor appetite for a technology that has attracted billions of dollars in investment and reshaped industries around the world.

Here is a look at the road to the blockbuster listing:

May 2021: 

Anthropic, led by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, announces it has raised $124 million in a Series A funding round led by technology investor and Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn. 

April 2022: 

Anthropic raises $580 million in a Series B funding round. 

March 2023: 

The company releases a large language model, Claude, that competes directly with offerings from OpenAI.            

May 2023: 

Anthropic raises $450 million from investors, including Alphabet's Google and Spark Capital.

September 2023: 

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) announces it will invest up to $4 billion in cash in Anthropic. 

October 2023: 

Alphabet's Google agrees to invest up to $2 billion in Anthropic.        

March 2024: 

Anthropic reveals a suite of AI models known as Claude 3. The company says the most capable in the family, Claude 3 Opus, outperforms rival models GPT-4 from OpenAI and Gemini 1.0 Ultra from Google on various benchmarks.

August 2024: 

Anthropic is hit with a class-action lawsuit in California federal court by three authors who say it misused their books and hundreds of thousands of others to train its AI-powered chatbot Claude.       

November 2024: 

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) pumps another $4 billion into Anthropic.             

March 2025: 

Anthropic raises $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion post-money valuation led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. 

September 2025: 

Anthropic's valuation hits $183 billion after raising $13 billion in a new round.  

September 2025: 

Anthropic unveils the Claude 4.5 AI model, saying the newest version can code for longer uninterrupted stretches and handle finance and scientific tasks better.          

February 2026: 

The company raises $30 billion in a funding round, more than doubling the Claude chatbot maker's valuation to $380 billion. 

February 2026: 

US President Donald Trump says he is directing the government to stop work with Anthropic, while the Pentagon said it would declare the startup a supply-chain risk.        

March 2026: 

Anthropic files a lawsuit to block the Pentagon from placing it on a national security blacklist, escalating the AI lab's high-stakes battle with the US military over usage restrictions on its technology.  

April 2026: 

Anthropic debuts Mythos, its most advanced AI model to date, equipped with sophisticated capabilities and designed for defensive cybersecurity tasks. The AI startup also announces "Project ‌Glasswing," under which select organizations will be allowed to use the AI model to find vulnerabilities in operating systems, web browsers and other software.

May 2026:    

Anthropic announces it has raised $65 billion at a valuation of $965 billion. 

June 2026: 

Anthropic confidentially files for a US IPO, edging ahead of rival OpenAI in a closely watched race to reach public markets.   

July 2026: 

A federal judge in San Francisco signs off on Anthropic's landmark $1.5 billion settlement of a class-action lawsuit brought by a group of authors who accused it of misusing their books to train its AI chatbot Claude.        

August 2026: 

Independent music publisher Round Hill Music sues Anthropic and Suno in California federal court, alleging the AI companies misused hundreds of its songs to ​train their systems.

August 2026: 

Anthropic projects 2028 revenue of ‌roughly $190 billion to $200 billion, Reuters reports, citing sources. 

August 2026: 

Anthropic's annual revenue run rate topped $65 billion by the end of July, Reuters reports, citing a source. 

October 2026:

Reuters reports, citing sources, that some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming IPO are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures.

October 2026:

Anthropic said it is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a public benefit corporation, a legal structure that requires management to balance broader public interests with profitability goals.

November 2026:

Anthropic plans to raise up to $64.4 billion in its US IPO after formally launching its roadshow.

November 2026:

Institutional investor interest in Anthropic's IPO outpaced the early days of SpaceX's roadshow, Reuters reports, citing sources.

November 2026:

Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market listing on record after upsizing its offering, valuing it at $1.5 trillion.

(Reporting by Manya Saini in Bengaluru; Editing by Sriraj Kalluvila, Subhranshu Sahu, Shinjini Ganguli and Leroy Leo)

data.title: Sterling drops from 20-month high versus euro
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Sterling pulled back from a 20-month high against the euro, though investors remained upbeat about the UK interest rate outlook and wary of headwinds facing the single currency ahead of key elections across Europe in 2027.

It edged lower against the greenback as the dollar index held near its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced a sweeping tariff package.

British inflation rose to a one-year high in October, data showed on Wednesday, and the Bank of England, responding to the data, said it "will continue to set interest rates to make sure inflation returns to the 2% target and stays there".

The euro rose 0.23% to 83.65 pence after hitting 83.20 pence on Wednesday, its lowest level since March 28, 2025.

Sterling fell 0.2% to $1.31475.

"We expect the euro/pound to hold around the 0.83 area on a 1-month view but see scope for a move down to the 0.82 area in the approach to the French Presidential election," Jane Foley, senior forex strategist at Rabobank, said.

Concerns about France's fiscal trajectory could weigh on the euro, but a market gauge of the risk premium investors demand to hold French debt has recently narrowed to around 150 basis points from a 15-year high of about 180 bps.

"A more hawkish Bank of England relative to the ECB over the coming months and PM Andy Burnham's efforts to get closer to Europe are two factors which should keep euro/pound offered," Chris Turner, head of forex strategy at ING, said.

Britain set out the broad shape of a package of agreements it hopes to strike with the European Union at a summit later this week, including a youth experience program, a food trade deal and closer cooperation on carbon emissions.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said that Britain's labour market no longer appeared to be loosening, although some slack remained.

BoE forecasts imply UK inflation will stay at or above 2% until the end of 2028, its longest such run since a 27-year stretch ended in 1994.

(reporting by Stefano Rebaudo; Editing by Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

data.title: UK's CMA says Viagogo may have broken the law on hidden ticket fees
data.description:
LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Britain's Competition and Markets Authority said on Thursday it had provisionally found that resale site Viagogo may have broken the law by failing to show consumers the total price upfront and adding fees.

The CMA said its finding was provisional and that it should not be assumed that Viagogo, owned by StubHub ( STUB ), had broken the law.

"This is an ongoing investigation and no final findings have been made," a Viagogo spokesperson said in a statement. "We have engaged constructively with the CMA and continue to cooperate fully with its investigation."

The CMA's probe focuses on a practice known as "drip pricing", often used for event tickets, where platforms advertise an initial price without including mandatory charges upfront and introducing unavoidable fees at checkout.

The CMA said that it believes mandatory costs such as taxes and booking fees were added at later stages of the checkout process and not included in the total price from the start.

data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed. 

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored." 

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: Stocks look to break losing streak ahead of blockbuster Anthropic IPO
data.description:
* Anthropic's blockbuster IPO pricing helps lifts Nasdaq futures Ongoing investor worries over AI trade linger

* Hawkish Fed lifts dollar to 19-month high, nudges up bond yields

(Updates throughout after European market open)

By Marc Jones and Ankur Banerjee

LONDON/SINGAPORE, Nov 19 (Reuters) - World stocks were in danger of setting their longest losing streak of the year on Thursday as bruised bulls pinned their hopes on Anthropic's blockbuster market debut later in the day to lift the otherwise fragile mood.

Asian markets hadn't fully read the script as Taiwan and Hong Kong both fell heavily overnight, but Europe's tech stocks quickly caught the thermal in early trading while Nasdaq futures jumped nearly 1.7% ahead of Wall Street's open.

Elsewhere, gold remained stuck near a 14-month low and benchmark government bond yields ticked up following talk of at least a further 50 basis points worth of US rate rises. But for the time being it was mostly background noise.

Claude-developer Anthropic's IPO is set to be the largest flotation of all time. Its shares were priced at a lofty $83 apiece, valuing the firm at about $1.5 trillion.

"At $83 per share, Anthropic is coming to market above its initial pricing range, but still below our $92 fair value estimate," said Malik Ahmed Khan, a senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

Khan said Anthropic would need to sustain rapid growth while managing the enormous cost of developing and running its models.

It is the first major developer to go public, so how it trades in the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinised to gauge the broader sentiment towards AI following the recent selloff in some parts of the market.

"The key question (for investors) is whether they are comfortable with that range of outcomes and have a sufficiently long-term horizon," Khan said.

OIL DIPS AGAIN

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were back under $92 a barrel, set for a third weekly fall.

Investors were also focusing on an unprecedented three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Asia.

The dollar was taking a breather after hitting a 19-month high this week. Hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday had bolstered expectations of another US rate hike in December.

The euro was at $1.0996, hovering near its lowest since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 159.48 per dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

Waller had said on CNBC that, if the Fed wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action", either through a half-point increase at the December meeting or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes at the start of next year.

The comments followed hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, which caused markets to brace for more rate hikes. Traders now price a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

The 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to 5.08% in European trading, dragging both German bund and UK gilt yields up fractionally too.

BERLIN'S BLESSING FOR UNICREDIT

As well as the excitement around Anthropic, Europe's traders also lifted both UniCredit and Commerzbank's shares as Berlin gave its blessing to the takeover of the German bank after years of resistance.

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken over the past few weeks by worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build related infrastructure.

Markets have mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, said the Anthropic IPO was a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won't settle the debate," she said. "There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it'll take a few things to climb it."

(Reporting by Marc Jones; Editing by Kevin Liffey)

data.title: Almost All Fed Officials See Need For Additional Rate Hikes, October Minutes Show
data.description:
03:29 PM EST, 11/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Almost all Federal Reserve officials agreed that interest rates must rise further to cool inflation, minutes from the central bank's October meeting showed Wednesday.

In a split vote on Oct. 28, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate steady after a 25-basis-point hike in September. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferred another quarter-percentage-point hike last month.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate -- broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections -- would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective," the minutes showed.

A couple of participants at the October meeting said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate by more than 25 basis points at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, according to the minutes.

US inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for nearly six years. Most participants at the October FOMC meeting viewed price pressures to be broad based and expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term, the minutes showed.

"Many participants viewed the (artificial intelligence) buildout as a material source of inflation risk," according to the minutes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday that the central bank may need to lift interest rates aggressively because inflation was "headed in the wrong direction."

The minutes showed a "stronger conviction in further hikes than (Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting) press conference conveyed, with disagreement mainly over timing, a message we have received from Fed speakers since this meeting," said Vikram Rai, senior economist at TD Economics.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that raising interest rates will be appropriate to bring inflation down to the 2% target in a timely manner, joining other central bank officials who have recently leaned hawkish.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the FOMC will likely need to lift its policy rate "several" times before spring. Hammack has also pushed for policy tightening, though she recently said that it must be undertaken gradually.

Markets widely expect the central bank to raise its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"A 25-basis-point December increase looks consistent with the broad consensus, but it is not assured, and a larger move is a conditional minority view," TD Economics' Rai said. "Broader inflation pass-through could require more restriction, while weaker AI investment and improving supply could limit it."

Shenzhen, China, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OBSBOT, an industry leader in smart videography technology, today officially unveiled OBSBOT Tail Air 2, an AI-powered PTZR camera designed for flexible video production. Combining a 1-inch CMOS sensor, 4K/60 imaging, OBSBOT Log, and Custom 3D LUTs, Tail Air 2 delivers professional-quality imaging with greater control over color and detail. AI Tracking 2.0, upgraded AI Director Grids, and automated camera movements reduce manual operation, while motorized PTZR, uncropped vertical 4K/60 recording, and native IP connectivity allow creators to adapt to different shooting setups, content formats, and multi-camera workflows.

“Creators shouldn't have to choose between image quality, creative control, and production efficiency,” said Liu Bo, CEO of OBSBOT. “With Tail Air 2, we're bringing these capabilities together, making professional-quality video production simpler and giving creators more freedom to focus on their content.”

A 1-Inch Sensor That Brings More to Every Frame

Tail Air 2 features a 1-inch CMOS sensor with 3.2 μm pixels, an f/1.9 aperture, and an eight-element optical lens. It captures detailed 4K footage at up to 60fps and 1080p video at up to 120fps, enabling creators to shoot crisp talking-head videos, capture fast-moving action, and produce smooth slow-motion footage in post-production.

A dedicated AI imaging chip achieves superior low-light performance by reducing noise while preserving fine details in low light. LOFIC HDR technology supports up to 13 stops of dynamic range[1] at frame rates up to 30fps, helping retain detail in bright highlights and dark shadows.

[1]The 13-stop dynamic range is achieved under HDR recording conditions. Actual performance may vary depending on recording settings and environmental conditions.

More Professional Control Over the Final Look with OBSBOT Log

Tail Air 2 introduces OBSBOT Log, the company's proprietary 8-bit Log recording profile and the first of its kind in an OBSBOT camera. By retaining tonal information across highlights and shadows, it provides greater latitude for color grading and post-production adjustments, giving creators more control over how their footage looks.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/7f48b3f7-5e34-4fa0-a98b-8f667999c88b/obsbot-tail-air3.png

Custom 3D LUT support lets creators preview different color treatments through OBSBOT Center, Obsbot Start and Obsbot Live. Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/43a72017-38d5-4e9b-b797-ab170d4a40d5/obsbot-tail-air4.png

AI Tracking That Follows Your Story

Whether a creator is teaching, demonstrating a product or presenting alone, Tail Air 2 is designed to keep the camera focused on the action with less manual intervention. AI Tracking 2.0 recognizes people, more than 30 animal species, and over 200 object categories. Users can simply double-click a subject or draw a selection box on the control interface to tell the camera what to track.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/3d55e51f-343f-408f-a528-3c9c6cf9973b/obsbot-tail-air5.png

Beyond recognizing and following a subject, AI Tracking 2.0 also adjusts framing to suit different shooting scenarios. Single-Person Tracking maintains focus on the selected subject, even when they are briefly obscured, and reacquires them when they return. Group Tracking adjusts the camera angle and framing as people move or enter and leave the shot, maintaining a balanced composition. Face Framing leaves sufficient space in the direction a subject faces, while Auto Zoom maintains the selected full-body, medium or close-up framing as the distance changes.

Creators can further tailor how the camera responds by adjusting tracking speed, selecting a single movement axis, setting active tracking zones and customizing subject positioning within the frame. Upgraded AI Director Grids bring these controls together, allowing creators to switch between AI Tracking, Preset, and Launchpad together in one intuitive interface. Gesture Control adds another layer of hands-free operation, allowing users to control tracking, zoom and recording from up to five meters away.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/b68bfa76-b1a5-4b8c-8bfb-0757ceb7dc66/obsbot-tail-air6.png

Together, these capabilities help creators manage subject tracking, framing and camera movements within a single workflow, making it easier to produce multi-shot content without a dedicated camera operator.

More Than PTZ: Creative Movement and Native Vertical 4K

Tail Air 2 expands traditional PTZ camera movement by introducing a dedicated Roll axis, adding rotation to its Pan, Tilt, and Zoom capabilities. This PTZR architecture gives creators more ways to control camera orientation, movement, and framing.

Launchpad 2.0 makes these creative camera movements easier to execute and repeat, with eight preset camera movements and two customizable modes that allow creators to tailor camera motion to their production needs. The Roll axis also enables an Auto Leveling System that automatically corrects camera orientation to keep the horizon level, even when the camera is mounted on an uneven surface.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/9d4b9699-2119-43ad-9138-c59c8b48d734/obsbot-tail-air7.png

For vertical content, Tail Air 2 physically rotates its lens module 90 degrees to capture native vertical 4K video at up to 60fps, without cropping the sensor's full imaging area. This allows creators to switch between landscape and vertical formats while retaining the full resolution of each shot.

Together, PTZR movement and native vertical imaging give creators more control over camera movement and framing across different production formats, from livestreams and long-form videos to vertical social content.

Designed for Modern Production Workflows and Multi-Camera Setups

Built around a native IP architecture, Tail Air 2 integrates into a wide range of production environments. It supports SRT, RTSP and RTMP protocols, along with NDI®|HX3 through the NDI-enabled version or a separately purchased license, with Wi-Fi 6 and wired Ethernet connectivity for network-based video transmission. VISCA, OSC, Stream Deck integration and an Open SDK further support camera control and customized workflows.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/27161571-3335-4c8a-adc4-6da9fdcc7d8d/obsbot-tail-air8.png

For more direct production setups, Tail Air 2 offers a 3.5mm audio input, Micro HDMI output and two USB-C ports for power and data. It also supports local recording to microSD cards up to 1TB, alongside its built-in microphone and Bluetooth connectivity with OBSBOT wireless microphone Vox SE.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/8317f1b5-a7ac-40a9-883b-91f504812be5/obsbot-tail-air9.png

Availability and Pricing
Tail Air 2 is offered in two versions: the Non-NDI version and the NDI version.
